breadcrumb: Post and panel sign concepts for property information
h1: Post and panel sign concepts for property information
lead: A post and panel sign places a defined message between or alongside supports, often near a property entrance or an approved temporary display area. The visible panel is only one part of the system: support, ground conditions and placement also determine whether the concept is appropriate. Vision Graphics can help New York property teams organize the graphic brief and compare information layouts. This page remains a review draft until the product offering and the site-specific fabrication, support and installation responsibilities have been confirmed.

sections.html: Prioritize the property name or main instruction, then give supporting information enough space to remain readable. If tenants or project details change, consider how the panel content could be updated without redesigning the full identity.

Document the proposed position, approach and surrounding conditions. Posts, foundations, utilities, exposure and permissions need appropriate review. An existing support system should not be assumed suitable for a different panel or a larger sign.

items.p: Present a concise name and directional message.
Organize several occupants within an approved panel layout.
Explore a defined panel for an authorized time-limited use.

items.q: Can the panel be changed later?
items.a_html: A replaceable panel can be considered, but the system should be specified for that purpose and reviewed for the site.
They are not assumed. The complete support and installation scope must be verified for the project.
